name: Driveshaft
description: Factory two-piece propeller shaft (rubber couplers each end, center support bearing) versus one-piece carbon/aluminum race shafts with CV front joint, plus safety loops and tunnel heat shield.

components.name: Front driveshaft section (factory two-piece)
components.description: Forward tube of the factory two-piece propeller shaft, from the transmission output coupler to the center support bearing. Factory shafts are balanced as an assembly - mark phasing before separating.
components.location: Tunnel from x≈1.27 (trans output) to x≈1.95 (center bearing), y≈0.34-0.36.

factory.name: GM two-piece propeller shaft assembly
factory.notes: 87839794 is listed for 2016-2024 Camaro LT1/SS; confirm manual vs auto and ZL1 application by VIN. Couplers generally sold only with the complete shaft.

specs.Construction: Two-piece with center support bearing, rubber couplers each end

hardware.notes: Value posted for the 5th-gen Camaro two-piece shaft (forum, from GM SI); coupler fasteners are described as torque-to-yield/one-time-use - confirm Gen 6 value in GM SI and replace bolts. Checked 2026-10: the TightTorque table compiled from the 2016-2018 Camaro service manual lists 'Front propeller shaft bolts 90 N·m (66 lb ft)'. The previous 67 ft-lb was the 5th-gen value. Replace the bolts and nuts.

installNotes: Mark 6 o'clock alignment on shaft and flanges before removal (QA1 procedure).
Support the shaft - it is heavy; slide off pilots using center-bearing play.

components.name: Center support (hanger) bearing
components.description: Rubber-isolated ball bearing in a bracket bolted under the tunnel that supports the joint between the two driveshaft halves. A torn isolator causes vibration and clunk.
components.location: Under tunnel at x≈1.95, y≈0.33, z=0, bracket bolted to tunnel crossmember/body.

factory.name: GM bearing assembly - propeller shaft center support

hardware.notes: QA1 instructions: two hanger-bearing bolts; value is an estimate. Checked 2026-10: the TightTorque table compiled from the 2016-2018 Camaro service manual lists 'Propeller shaft bearing bolts 50 N·m (37 lb ft)'. GM bulletin 19-NA-266 confirms the 2016+ LT1/LT4 two-piece shaft uses a center support bearing.

installNotes: Leave bolts loose until both couplers are torqued, then center the bearing and torque.

components.name: Front flex coupler (guibo) - trans end
components.description: Rubber/fabric flex disc between the trans output flange and the front driveshaft (3 bolts each side, alternating). Absorbs shock and minor angle; it is a wear item that tears under race launches and heat.
components.location: At transmission output flange, x≈1.27, y≈0.36.

factory.name: GM rubber coupler (flex joint)
factory.notes: Generally supplied with the driveshaft assembly only.

hardware.notes: Value posted for the 5th-gen Camaro two-piece shaft (forum, from GM SI); coupler fasteners are described as torque-to-yield/one-time-use - confirm Gen 6 value in GM SI and replace bolts. installNotes: Install arrows/markings on coupler per GM orientation.
inspection: Cracks/tears in rubber between bolt holes every event

components.name: One-piece race driveshaft (carbon or aluminum)
components.description: Single-tube carbon-fiber or aluminum shaft replacing the two-piece factory shaft, center bearing and couplers. Cuts rotating mass and removes the flex discs that wrap up and fail on track. Carbon shafts fail by delaminating into fibers rather than flailing a steel tube.
components.location: Tunnel from trans output (x≈1.27) to pinion flange (x≈2.61), y≈0.35.

raceOptions.name: DSS carbon fiber 1-piece, 3.25 in (2016-17 Camaro SS manual)
raceOptions.notes: Direct bolt-in for factory trans and rear end; built and balanced to order. Separate versions exist for automatic and for ZL1 - confirm application.

raceOptions.name: QA1 REV Series carbon fiber driveshaft (2016-2018 Camaro SS manual)
raceOptions.notes: Front CV + aluminum flange adapter; SFI-certified per vendor listing.

specs.Front CV installed length check (QA1): 2-9/16 to 2-7/8 in from CV to shaft

hardware.item: Rear flange-to-pinion flange bolt with nut (QA1, 6th gen)
hardware.torqueSequence: Snug first ensuring flange fully seated in pinion pilot; torque after front is complete

installNotes: Clean pinion and trans flange mating faces of dirt, grease and corrosion.
Install the CV flange adapter to the trans output flange first (see cv-flange-adapter).
Snug rear flange to pinion with blue threadlocker, ensuring it seats fully in the pilot.
Bolt CV to adapter (6 x M10, 47 ft-lb) matching color codes.
Torque pinion bolts to 85 ft-lb with parking brake applied.
Measure CV-to-shaft dimension 2-9/16 to 2-7/8 in; reshape tunnel heat shield rear edge for clearance; rotate and check clearance to exhaust.
Wash carbon shafts with soap and water only.

components.name: Driveshaft safety loop(s)
components.description: Steel hoop(s) bolted to the floor/crossmember around the driveshaft that prevent a failed shaft from pole-vaulting the car or entering the cockpit. Many road-race rulebooks (NASA, SCCA and others) require a loop near the front joint for cars with exposed driveshafts - check your class rules for count and placement.
components.location: Around shaft just behind trans output (x≈1.40) and optionally near center (x≈2.00), bolted to tunnel/crossmember.

raceOptions.name: Bolt-in or fabricated 360° loop, 1/4 x 2 in steel strap or 7/8 in tube
raceOptions.notes: Size to clear shaft by ~1 in all around through suspension travel.

specs.Typical section: ≥1/4 x 2 in strap or ≥7/8 x .120 tube (check rules)

hardware.spec: 3/8-16 or M10 Gr 8/10.9 with large washers / backing plates

installNotes: Fit after driveshaft is final; check clearance at full droop/compression.
inspection: Witness marks from shaft contact (indicates vibration/failure)

sources.title: QA1 REV Series carbon driveshaft install instructions 9919-230 ('10-'18 Camaro SS, JJ-22207/JJ-22208)

modelRef.features: 360-degree steel loop with tabs bolted to the floor

components.name: Tunnel heat shield
components.description: Reflective shield in the tunnel above the driveshaft and exhaust. Protects the floor, shift boot and (on composite shafts) the carbon tube from exhaust heat. QA1 notes the rear edge must be reshaped downward for its CF shaft clearance - so 'downward' clearance to shaft must be rechecked.

raceOptions.name: Gold/ceramic reflective film or stamped aluminum shield

installNotes: Reinstall after driveshaft and exhaust; check shaft clearance through rotation.
